info.name: sandbox-runner
info.description:
sandbox-runner endpoints, called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/sandbox` → `http://sandbox-runner:8000`, `include_subpath: true`). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key. Set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` (an sk-… key issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys) — every request inherits them via collection-level auth. See ai/sandbox/ENDPOINTS.md for the full endpoint reference and ai/litellm/LITELLM.md for issuing virtual keys.

Sessions: POST /run supports an optional `session_id` for persistent previews across turns. First call: omit `session_id`; server generates one and returns it. Follow-up call: pass the same `session_id` back — server writes new files into the running container's /app, returns the same URL, dev server hot-reloads. Set the `sandboxSessionId` collection variable from the first response, then run the 'update in-session' request. See ai/sandbox/SANDBOX.md § Sessions.

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). Scope the key to allow the /v1/sandbox pass-through — most keys created for chat models already do. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth.

12-char hex id returned by POST /run as `sandbox_id`. Fill in after spawning to run the /jobs/{id} + DELETE /jobs/{id} requests. This changes on every spawn — for a stable handle across turns use `sandboxSessionId`.

Persistent session handle returned by POST /run as `session_id`. Paste it here and it's used by the 'update in-session' + 'delete files' + 'DELETE /session' requests below. Passing the same value back to POST /run updates the running container's files in place — same URL, dev server hot-reloads.

MCP transport session id — paste in the `mcp-session-id` response header value returned by the `MCP — initialize` request. Subsequent MCP calls need it. UNRELATED to `sandboxSessionId` — this one is FastMCP's HTTP-transport session cookie, not the sandbox reuse handle.

request.description: Liveness + DB status. Returns {"status": "ok", "db": "up"} when the runner can reach sandbox-db; "degraded" / "down" otherwise.

Spawn a static HTML sandbox — nginx serves the files map at /. Returns { sandbox_id, session_id, url, expires_at, reused, runtime, startup_output, tests }. The URL uses whatever SANDBOX_PROXY_URL is set to in .env — for browser-reachable iframes, that should be a public URL under the same origin as Open WebUI (e.g. https://chat.zeoenergy.com/sandboxes).

**Tests required.** The body must include at least one file under `tests/`; the request above adds `tests/run.sh` (POSIX shell + curl using $PREVIEW_URL) which the sandbox-tester container executes against the live preview before the response returns. On a green run the response body's `tests.ok` is true. Copy the returned `session_id` into the `sandboxSessionId` collection variable to run the 'update in-session' request afterwards — tests persist across turns, so follow-ups don't have to re-send tests/run.sh.

body.raw:
{
  "runtime": "python",
  "files": {
    "app.py": "import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

st.title('sine wave demo')
n = st.slider('samples', 10, 500, 100)
freq = st.slider('frequency', 1, 10, 3)
x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n)
df = pd.DataFrame({'x': x, 'y': np.sin(freq * x)})
st.line_chart(df.set_index('x'))
",
    "tests/test_ui.py": "import os
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright, expect


def test_title_renders():
    url = os.environ['PREVIEW_URL']
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch()
        page = browser.new_page()
        page.goto(url)
        expect(page.get_by_text('sine wave demo')).to_be_visible(timeout=15000)
        browser.close()
"
  },
  "ttl_seconds": 900
}

request.description:
Spawn a Streamlit sandbox. Runtime `python` base image has streamlit, gradio, flask, fastapi, pandas, numpy, matplotlib, plotly, requests, pillow pre-installed. Add a requirements.txt to files to install additional deps via sandbox-egress (pypi allowlisted). Cold-start ~2s pre-baked; 20-90s if pip install runs.

The request body includes a `tests/test_ui.py` that uses Playwright + chromium (pre-installed in the sandbox-tester image) to navigate the live Streamlit URL and assert the title is visible. Expect the response's `tests.duration_s` to add ~10-15s on a cold Playwright launch — bump SANDBOX_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS if the default 60s is tight.

Illustrates the install-if-present pattern. If files contains a requirements.txt, the base image entrypoint runs `pip install -r requirements.txt` before executing the command. pip goes through HTTP_PROXY=sandbox-egress:8888 and hits the pypi.org / files.pythonhosted.org allowlist.

Spawn a Node sandbox. Base image has serve, vite, react, react-dom, express, next installed globally so `require('express')` works without a package.json. Add a package.json to files to trigger `npm install` on boot.
Multi-file Vite + React counter. Vite HMR uses WebSockets — sandbox-proxy (Caddy) forwards them by default, so buttons work end-to-end when iframed.

Update a preview in place. Pass the `session_id` from a previous /run response (via the sandboxSessionId collection variable) and the file(s) that changed. The runner writes them into the running container's /app via docker cp — no respawn. Response has `reused: true` and the SAME sandbox_id + url as the initial spawn. The dev server inside the sandbox reloads on file change: nginx serves the new file on next request, Streamlit auto-reruns, Vite HMR fires without a browser refresh. If the container was already reaped when this call arrives (idle-TTL or manual rm), the runner self-heals — same session_id, new sandbox_id, new url — so callers don't have to distinguish the two cases.

`files` is treated as an overlay: paths listed here overwrite the running container's copies; unlisted files stay put. Save tokens by not resending unchanged files.

Confirms the tests-required gate — the body includes no file under `tests/`, so the runner refuses with HTTP 400 before spawning anything. The response body's `detail` is `{error: "tests missing", session_id, runtime, hint, example}` where `example` is a minimal working test file the model can copy. Passing this expectation confirms `SANDBOX_TESTS_REQUIRED=true`. To disable the gate for a migration window, set `SANDBOX_TESTS_REQUIRED=false` in .env and this call will succeed instead.

Explicitly remove file(s) from a running sandbox. Use on follow-up calls when the model renames or drops a file — otherwise stale files linger, because overlay semantics on `files` never delete. Paths are relative to /app; absolute paths and '..' return 400. Combine with a `files` map to atomically add + remove in one call.

Ignored on the first call (no session_id) — the container starts fresh from `files` alone, there's nothing to delete.

variable.description: Persistent session handle returned by POST /run as session_id.

request.description:
Explicitly tear down the running sandbox for a session. Idempotent — returns 204 whether or not the session existed. Distinct from DELETE /jobs/{sandbox_id}: /jobs targets a specific spawn event by its 12-char internal id, while /session targets whatever's currently running under the persistent session handle (may have been respawned via self-heal since the model last saw it). Useful in tests and cleanup scripts; models rarely need it because the reaper's idle-TTL sweep handles silent chats on its own.

Errors: 400 if session_id fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`, 500 if the runner isn't initialized.

variable.description: Persistent session handle returned by POST /run as session_id.

request.description:
Stream the running sandbox's /app back as a tar archive (Content-Type: application/x-tar, Content-Disposition: attachment). Docker daemon does the packing (container.get_archive) so nothing buffers in the runner. Session-based, so this URL keeps working across self-heal spawns — resolves session_id → current container at request time.

Also exposed publicly via the sandbox-proxy Caddy route at ${SANDBOX_PROXY_URL}/download/{sandboxSessionId} (e.g. https://chat.zeoenergy.com/sandboxes/download/…) so browsers can download the archive with the same oauth2-proxy auth as the preview iframe. preview_app's response text includes this URL on the 'Download source:' line — models share it verbatim when a user asks to save the code.

Errors: 400 if session_id fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`, 404 if there's no running sandbox for this session (never existed, or reaped without self-heal).

Postman note: click 'Send and Download' to save the response as a file. The tar root is `app/`, so `tar -xf sandbox-*.tar` extracts to `./app/`.

query.description: Trailing lines to return. Default 100, clamped 1..1000.

variable.description: Persistent session handle returned by POST /run as session_id.

request.description:
Return the last N lines of the running sandbox's stdout+stderr. Session-based so this follows self-heal.

How the logs get there: the runner's two-phase spawn runs the user command via `docker exec` (detached), not as PID 1 (`sleep infinity` is PID 1). container.logs() only sees PID 1's streams, so exec output isn't captured there. The spawn redirects the user command to /tmp/sandbox.log (128 MB tmpfs), and this endpoint runs `tail -n N` inside the container to read it back.

Which runtimes surface useful output here: Flask (`app.run`), FastAPI + uvicorn, Express, Vite, Next, and any bare `python app.py` all print tracebacks to stdout. STREAMLIT is the exception — it catches user exceptions and renders them in the browser rather than printing to stdout, so this endpoint shows only the 'You can now view your Streamlit app…' banner. For Streamlit apps, inspect the rendered HTML from the sandbox URL to see error text.

Response (200): {session_id, sandbox_id, lines_requested, logs}. Empty `logs` string means either the container just spawned and hasn't printed anything yet, or the app writes to a file — NOT a failure signal.

Errors: 400 if session_id fails the regex, 404 if there's no running sandbox for this session.

List every sandbox in the registry (running + terminal). Fixed limit of 20 in PostgresRegistry.list_all(). Ordered by updated_at DESC. Returns JobsListResponse — see ENDPOINTS.md for the JobBase shape. `metadata->>'session_id'` on each job shows the persistent handle a sandbox was spawned under; multiple 'running' rows can share a session_id only briefly (during self-heal), the reaper normalizes.

variable.description: 12-char hex id returned by POST /run as sandbox_id.

request.description: Snapshot of one sandbox. 404 if unknown. Set the sandboxId collection variable to the id returned by POST /run first.

variable.description: 12-char hex id returned by POST /run as sandbox_id.

request.description:
Direct download by internal sandbox_id — bypasses session resolution. Useful for operators who want to grab the archive from a SPECIFIC spawn event even if the session self-healed to a different container since. Same tar shape as the session variant. Prefer /session/{id}/download for end-user download links because that URL keeps working across self-heal.

Errors: 404 if no sandbox with that id, 409 if the sandbox exists in the registry but never reached the `running` phase (no container to export).

variable.description: 12-char hex id returned by POST /run as sandbox_id.

request.description:
Direct log fetch by internal sandbox_id. Useful when the session self-healed to a new container but you want the previous container's output. Same underlying mechanism as /session/{id}/logs (tails /tmp/sandbox.log inside the container). Response body: {sandbox_id, lines_requested, logs}.

Errors: 404 if no sandbox with that id, 409 if the sandbox never reached the `running` phase — no container to read logs from.

variable.description: 12-char hex id returned by POST /run as sandbox_id.

request.description: Tear a sandbox down early. Stops the container, removes it, deletes the row, releases the concurrency slot. Returns 204 no body. 404 if the sandbox id is unknown.

item.name: MCP
item.description: FastMCP JSON-RPC over HTTP forwarded through the LiteLLM pass-through. Note that LiteLLM ALSO advertises the sandbox as an MCP server via `mcp_servers.sandbox` in litellm_config.yaml — models see the tool through that path, not this one. The Postman requests below are useful for debugging the transport directly. Every MCP request MUST use trailing-slash (POST /mcp/), MUST send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, and MUST start with an `initialize` call — copy the `mcp-session-id` response header into the `mcpSessionId` collection variable for subsequent calls.

request.description: MCP handshake. Response headers include `mcp-session-id` — copy it into the `mcpSessionId` collection variable.
Enumerate available tools. sandbox-runner exposes exactly one: preview_app.

Invoke preview_app via MCP. Result body has a text-content block containing a fenced ```html code block with a self-contained HTML document ready for OpenWebUI's artifacts split-panel (`ContentRenderer.svelte` promotes it via `['html','svg'].includes(normalizedLang)`). The document uses meta-refresh + JS fallback to navigate OpenWebUI's srcdoc iframe to the running sandbox URL — no nested iframe.

Invoke preview_app for a Python (Streamlit) sandbox via MCP. Response text starts with `Preview ready.` followed by a `Session id: XYZ` line — the model uses that value verbatim in the next call to update the same preview.

Follow-up preview_app call reusing an existing session_id. Response text starts with `Preview updated.` instead of `Preview ready.` and contains the same URL — the running Streamlit process detects the file-change and reruns automatically, no browser refresh needed. Save the sandboxSessionId variable first: run the streamlit call above, copy the Session id from its response, paste into the collection variable, then run this.

item.name: MCP — tools/call preview_app (SYNTAX ERROR — see feedback)

request.description:
Demonstrates the static-lint feedback loop. The Python file has an unclosed `st.title(` call and an incomplete `def broken(`. Before touching Docker, the runner compiles every .py file with Python's built-in `compile()` — SyntaxError is caught in ~1 ms and returned to the model as a compiler-style diagnostic:

    preview_app failed: static lint failed
    Session id: <fresh-id>

    Static lint found 1 error(s):
      app.py:3:1: SyntaxError: invalid syntax
        def broken(
        ^

    Fix the syntax errors above and call preview_app again with the same session_id. No container was spawned.

Model reads the diagnostic, fixes the code, and calls preview_app again with the same session_id — the session-reuse path handles the retry transparently. No container was spawned so no slot was consumed.

item.name: MCP — tools/call preview_app (RUNTIME ERROR — see feedback)

request.description:
Demonstrates the runtime-error feedback loop. The Python file passes static lint (syntax is valid) but imports a non-existent module — the container spawns, fails at import time, never binds port 80, and the 30 s readiness probe expires. Before tearing the container down, the runner reads /tmp/sandbox.log and returns the traceback to the model:

    preview_app failed: sandbox did not become ready within 30s
    Session id: <fresh-id>

    Container logs (last 100 lines):
    ---
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "/app/app.py", line 2, in <module>
        import this_module_does_not_exist
    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'this_module_does_not_exist'
    ---

    Read the container logs above… Fix the code and call preview_app again with the same session_id.

This takes ~30 s (waiting for the readiness timeout). Static lint catches syntax errors instantly; runtime errors require the full spawn.

On-demand log fetch for a running sandbox. Use this when preview_app already returned a normal ready/updated response but the user reports the app looks broken (Flask/FastAPI/Vite/Next tracebacks all print here before the browser renders an error card).

Do NOT call this after a preview_app FAILURE — those already include the container logs in the tool response. Only call when the container is running but its output looks wrong.

Set the sandboxSessionId collection variable to the session_id from a previous preview_app response, then run this. Returns formatted text or an explicit 'no logs available' message.

STREAMLIT NOTE: Streamlit catches user exceptions and renders them in the browser, not stdout. For Streamlit apps this shows only the startup banner. For everything else, this is where the traceback is.
